verdict.rationale: x402 doesn't issue traditional scoped API credentials (it explicitly removes API keys in favor of pay-per-request), but it does provide functionally analogous least-privilege mechanisms for agents: the 'upto' scheme lets a buyer authorize a maximum spend and settle only what was used, agentic wallets/accounts hold funds the agent can spend, and batch settlement vouchers carry cryptographically signed limits with defined refund/withdrawal semantics. This addresses spend-scoping for agents but not general API permission scoping (e.g., resource/action-level access control). Missing for 10: explicit credential/token issuance with granular resource or action scopes beyond spend caps, and independent hands-on verification of the limit-enforcement mechanics.
